# Glossary

The glossary defines the words the manual uses for Regia Engine. Edit `docs/manual/glossary.ron` and run `cargo xtask manual`; this page is generated. Terms are ordered by their spelling, ignoring case. See-also links jump to another term on this page.

## A

### Agent protocol

The JSON protocol a dev build serves so a tool can inspect and drive a running app. The app writes an endpoint file when it starts.

See also: [Play in editor](#play-in-editor).

Page: [../agents/protocol.md](../agents/protocol.md).

### Anim graph

A graph that blends animation clips and drives a skeleton. The cook writes the runtime graph from the source file.

See also: [Character](#character).

Page: [../user-guide/animation.md#anim-graphs](../user-guide/animation.md#anim-graphs).

### Asset id

The stable id stored in a source asset's .meta sidecar. It does not change when the file moves, and levels refer to assets by this id.

See also: [Cook](#cook), [Asset server](#asset-server).

Page: [../fundamentals/assets.md#meta-sidecars-and-asset-ids](../fundamentals/assets.md#meta-sidecars-and-asset-ids).

### Asset server

The AssetServer resource loads cooked assets by project path or id, from mounted pak archives first and then from the cook cache.

See also: [Cook](#cook), [Pak](#pak), [Asset id](#asset-id).

Page: [../fundamentals/assets.md#loading-cooked-assets](../fundamentals/assets.md#loading-cooked-assets).

## C

### Character

The body a controller drives. A player controller is the human; an AI controller drives a bot. Gameplay code spawns the character with a movement component.

See also: [Prediction](#prediction), [Anim graph](#anim-graph).

Page: [../user-guide/gameplay.md](../user-guide/gameplay.md).

### Client

A net mode that joins a server. It sends inputs and receives replicated state.

See also: [Dedicated server](#dedicated-server), [Prediction](#prediction).

Page: [../user-guide/networking.md#client](../user-guide/networking.md#client).

### Component

A plain Rust value attached to an entity, such as a transform or a health value. A marker component carries no fields and exists so a system can filter on it.

See also: [Entity](#entity), [ECS world](#ecs-world).

Page: [../fundamentals/ecs.md#components](../fundamentals/ecs.md#components).

### Content format

A frozen on-disk shape for game content, with a version field. A loader rejects a newer version and runs migrators for an older one.

See also: [Migrator](#migrator), [Cook](#cook).

Page: [../changing-a-content-format.md](../changing-a-content-format.md).

### Cook

The step that turns source assets into the compact data the runtime loads. It is incremental: an output is rebuilt only when its source, import settings or importer version changed.

See also: [Package](#package), [Asset id](#asset-id), [Cooked mesh](#cooked-mesh).

Page: [../fundamentals/assets.md#what-the-cook-does](../fundamentals/assets.md#what-the-cook-does).

### Cooked mesh

The mesh the cook writes for a glTF primitive, including its LODs. With meshlets enabled, the cook also writes a cluster file that indexes that mesh's vertices.

See also: [Cook](#cook), [Meshlet](#meshlet).

Page: [../agents/visbuffer.md#cooking-meshlets](../agents/visbuffer.md#cooking-meshlets).

## D

### DDGI

The dynamic global-illumination field: camera-relative cascades of irradiance probes that trace the terrain heightfield and per-mesh distance fields, with Chebyshev visibility so light does not pass through closed walls.

See also: [Probe volume](#probe-volume), [Quality tier](#quality-tier).

Page: [../agents/dynamic-gi.md](../agents/dynamic-gi.md).

### Dedicated server

A net mode that hosts with no local players, no rendering and no audio. Packaging a server build produces that process.

See also: [Listen server](#listen-server), [Client](#client), [Package](#package).

Page: [../user-guide/networking.md#modes-transports-and-finding-a-game](../user-guide/networking.md#modes-transports-and-finding-a-game).

## E

### ECS world

The data of a running game lives in one world: entities, the components on them, the systems that read and write those components, and singleton resources.

See also: [Entity](#entity), [Component](#component), [System](#system), [Schedule](#schedule).

Page: [../fundamentals/ecs.md](../fundamentals/ecs.md).

### Entity

An id with no data of its own. What an entity is comes from the components attached to it.

See also: [Component](#component), [ECS world](#ecs-world).

Page: [../fundamentals/ecs.md#the-ecs-entities-components-systems](../fundamentals/ecs.md#the-ecs-entities-components-systems).

## F

### FixedUpdate

The schedule for simulation that must not depend on frame rate. It runs at FixedTime::hz (default 60), as many times as the accumulated time requires, and at most max\_substeps times in one frame (default 5, hard cap 64).

See also: [Schedule](#schedule), [Update](#update).

Page: [../fundamentals/app-and-plugins.md#time-and-the-fixed-timestep](../fundamentals/app-and-plugins.md#time-and-the-fixed-timestep).

### Frame

One pass of the app, from the clocks through the render graph and present. A paused clock still runs Update. FixedUpdate runs only when a fixed step is due.

See also: [Schedule](#schedule), [FixedUpdate](#fixedupdate).

Page: [../fundamentals/app-and-plugins.md#the-frame](../fundamentals/app-and-plugins.md#the-frame).

## H

### Hot reload

A dev build that watches the cook cache reloads a cooked file in place when the cook rewrites it. The next frame uses the new data.

See also: [Cook](#cook), [Play in editor](#play-in-editor).

Page: [../fundamentals/assets.md#hot-reload-of-assets](../fundamentals/assets.md#hot-reload-of-assets).

## I

### Input

The actions a player produces. The frame turns platform events into input state before gameplay systems read it.

See also: [Character](#character), [FixedUpdate](#fixedupdate).

Page: [../user-guide/input.md](../user-guide/input.md).

## J

### Join code

A short code the relay gives a host. Another client joins with that code instead of with an address.

See also: [Relay](#relay).

Page: [../agents/net-relay.md#join-by-code-the-clients-codes](../agents/net-relay.md#join-by-code-the-clients-codes).

## L

### Level

A scene file the editor saves and the game loads: entities with stable ids, names and reflected components. The loader migrates an older scene version in memory.

See also: [Scene](#scene), [Prefab](#prefab).

Page: [../user-guide/scenes.md#levels](../user-guide/scenes.md#levels).

### Lightmap

Baked irradiance stored per texel for the static meshes of a map. The level names the lightmap, or the renderer installs it, and the receivers shade with it.

See also: [Probe volume](#probe-volume), [Cook](#cook).

Page: [../agents/lightmaps.md](../agents/lightmaps.md).

### Listen server

A net mode that hosts the session and also has local players. The same process simulates and renders.

See also: [Dedicated server](#dedicated-server), [Client](#client), [Net mode](#net-mode).

Page: [../user-guide/networking.md#modes-transports-and-finding-a-game](../user-guide/networking.md#modes-transports-and-finding-a-game).

### Lobby hub

A self-hosted process that gives games lobbies, a directory, presence and invites. Clients talk to it with the hub lobby backend.

See also: [Relay](#relay), [Dedicated server](#dedicated-server).

Page: [../agents/net-lobby-hub.md](../agents/net-lobby-hub.md).

### Lockstep

A simulation in which every peer runs the same inputs through the same math and gets the same state. Lockstep code stays on integer and deterministic operations.

See also: [Rollback](#rollback), [FixedUpdate](#fixedupdate).

Page: [../agents/lockstep-math.md](../agents/lockstep-math.md).

## M

### Material

The surface description a mesh shades with. A source material cooks into the runtime material and references cooked textures.

See also: [Cook](#cook), [Cooked mesh](#cooked-mesh).

Page: [../user-guide/materials.md](../user-guide/materials.md).

### Meshlet

A small cluster of triangles built over LOD 0 of a cooked mesh. The visibility-buffer path draws these clusters.

See also: [Visibility buffer](#visibility-buffer), [Cooked mesh](#cooked-mesh).

Page: [../agents/visbuffer.md#cooking-meshlets](../agents/visbuffer.md#cooking-meshlets).

### Migrator

A registered step that reads one older content-format version and writes the next. A version bump ships with a migrator, and upgrade-project can rewrite the files on disk.

See also: [Content format](#content-format).

Page: [../changing-a-content-format.md](../changing-a-content-format.md).

## N

### Net mode

Which role a process runs: Offline, ListenServer, DedicatedServer or Client. Offline is the default.

See also: [Client](#client), [Listen server](#listen-server), [Dedicated server](#dedicated-server).

Page: [../user-guide/networking.md#modes-transports-and-finding-a-game](../user-guide/networking.md#modes-transports-and-finding-a-game).

### Net wire version

The number REGIA\_NET\_WIRE\_VERSION (6) stamped on a connection. A peer on another wire, another protocol hash or another content manifest is refused.

See also: [Client](#client), [Dedicated server](#dedicated-server).

Page: [../user-guide/networking.md#when-versions-or-content-differ](../user-guide/networking.md#when-versions-or-content-differ).

## P

### Package

A shipped build. The package command cooks when the archives are stale and writes the cooked data beside the executable.

See also: [Pak](#pak), [Cook](#cook).

Page: [../user-guide/packaging.md](../user-guide/packaging.md).

### Pak

A packed archive of cooked assets (.fpak). A packaged game reads the same cooked data from these archives that a development game reads from the cook cache.

See also: [Package](#package), [Asset server](#asset-server).

Page: [../fundamentals/assets.md#packaging](../fundamentals/assets.md#packaging).

### Play in editor

The editor copies the edit world into a separate play world and runs it. Play does not write back to the edit world.

See also: [Agent protocol](#agent-protocol), [Hot reload](#hot-reload).

Page: [../start/editor-tour.md#play-in-editor](../start/editor-tour.md#play-in-editor).

### Plugin

A type that implements Plugin. Its build method adds systems, resources, messages and other plugins to the app.

See also: [Schedule](#schedule), [ECS world](#ecs-world).

Page: [../fundamentals/app-and-plugins.md#plugins](../fundamentals/app-and-plugins.md#plugins).

### Prediction

The client simulates its own character ahead of the server and corrects when the server's state arrives.

See also: [Rollback](#rollback), [Client](#client).

Page: [../user-guide/networking.md#predicting-your-own-character-spec-73](../user-guide/networking.md#predicting-your-own-character-spec-73).

### Prefab

An entity subtree saved for reuse. Spawning an instance applies overrides on top of the template and does not edit the template.

See also: [Level](#level), [Scene](#scene).

Page: [../user-guide/scenes.md#prefabs](../user-guide/scenes.md#prefabs).

### Probe volume

A grid of irradiance probes (a GiField) that store the light arriving from every direction. Inside the grid the probes replace the sky term.

See also: [DDGI](#ddgi), [Lightmap](#lightmap).

Page: [../systems/lighting.md#indirect-light](../systems/lighting.md#indirect-light).

## Q

### Quality tier

The graphics budget automatic quality detection picks for a machine, from VeryLow through Ultra, plus Deck and the mobile presets. Each tier selects a render profile and a frame-rate target.

See also: [Render profile](#render-profile), [DDGI](#ddgi).

Page: [../user-guide/auto-quality.md#tiers](../user-guide/auto-quality.md#tiers).

## R

### Reflection probe

A captured environment the renderer uses when a screen-space reflection misses. The renderer picks a short list of probes by distance from the camera.

See also: [Lightmap](#lightmap), [Probe volume](#probe-volume).

Page: [../systems/lighting.md#reflections](../systems/lighting.md#reflections).

### Relay

A process that forwards datagrams between a host and clients that cannot reach each other directly. A dedicated server can publish a relay and a join code.

See also: [Join code](#join-code), [Lobby hub](#lobby-hub).

Page: [../agents/net-relay.md](../agents/net-relay.md).

### Render graph

The frame's passes in recording order, with the resources each pass reads and writes. A game adds a pass at a named slot, and the frame still submits once.

See also: [Render profile](#render-profile), [Frame](#frame).

Page: [../agents/render-graph.md](../agents/render-graph.md).

### Render profile

A named bundle of quality settings, such as MobileLow, DesktopHigh, DesktopUltra or Deck. A game installs one through RenderSettings.

See also: [Quality tier](#quality-tier), [Render graph](#render-graph).

Page: [../user-guide/rendering.md#render-profiles](../user-guide/rendering.md#render-profiles).

### Resource

A singleton value stored in the world, such as the clock or the asset server. There is one of each resource type.

See also: [ECS world](#ecs-world), [Asset server](#asset-server).

Page: [../fundamentals/ecs.md#resources](../fundamentals/ecs.md#resources).

### Rollback

A lockstep mode that steps ahead with predicted inputs and replays from the first tick whose real inputs differ when the frame arrives. Only confirmed ticks are hashed.

See also: [Lockstep](#lockstep), [Prediction](#prediction).

Page: [../agents/net-lockstep.md#rollback-lockstep](../agents/net-lockstep.md#rollback-lockstep).

## S

### Save game

A file under the user mount that stores a player's progress. The gameplay layer reads and writes it through the virtual file system.

See also: [Level](#level), [Scene](#scene).

Page: [../user-guide/gameplay.md](../user-guide/gameplay.md).

### Scene

The text files that store levels and prefabs. Re-saving an unchanged level writes the same bytes.

See also: [Level](#level), [Prefab](#prefab).

Page: [../user-guide/scenes.md](../user-guide/scenes.md).

### Schedule

A named stage of the frame that runs a set of systems. The frame runs Startup, First, PreUpdate, FixedUpdate, Update, PostUpdate, Extract, Render and Last, and StateTransition around them.

See also: [FixedUpdate](#fixedupdate), [Update](#update), [Frame](#frame).

Page: [../fundamentals/app-and-plugins.md#the-frame](../fundamentals/app-and-plugins.md#the-frame).

### System

A Rust function the frame runs to read and write components and resources. Which systems run, and in what order, is the schedule they were added to.

See also: [Schedule](#schedule), [ECS world](#ecs-world).

Page: [../fundamentals/ecs.md#systems-and-queries](../fundamentals/ecs.md#systems-and-queries).

## U

### Update

The schedule that runs most gameplay once per frame, after FixedUpdate and before PostUpdate.

See also: [Schedule](#schedule), [FixedUpdate](#fixedupdate).

Page: [../fundamentals/app-and-plugins.md#the-frame](../fundamentals/app-and-plugins.md#the-frame).

## V

### VFS

The virtual file system every engine file access goes through. Mounts include assets, config, user, cache and logs. Only the user and cache mounts are writable.

See also: [Package](#package), [Asset server](#asset-server).

Page: [../fundamentals/assets.md#where-files-live-the-vfs](../fundamentals/assets.md#where-files-live-the-vfs).

### Visibility buffer

A render path that records which primitive covers each pixel and shades afterwards. A glTF cooks meshlet clusters when its .meta sets meshlets.

See also: [Meshlet](#meshlet), [Render profile](#render-profile).

Page: [../agents/visbuffer.md](../agents/visbuffer.md).
